clinician.trajectory_summary: An 83-year-old male presented to the Emergency Department with acute per-rectal bleeding and syncope. He had a history of acute cholecystitis 5 weeks prior that was managed conservatively with planned elective cholecystectomy. On admission, vital signs were stable (BP 134/82, HR 86, RR 22, Temp 36.3°C). Physical examination was unremarkable except for the documented per-rectal bleeding. Laboratory studies showed hemoglobin of 11.9 mg/dL on admission, declining to 10.2 mg/dL within 24 hours, indicating ongoing blood loss. CT abdomen performed on the day of admission identified a 6 mm cystic artery pseudoaneurysm as the source of bleeding. The pseudoaneurysm was treated with endovascular coil embolization of the cystic artery performed by the interventional radiologist and attending surgeon. The procedure was well tolerated with unremarkable post-procedure recovery. The patient remained pain-free with no further per-rectal bleeding during hospitalization and was discharged 24 hours post-embolization. Follow-up week at home was unremarkable. Follow-up contrast-enhanced CT performed approximately 4 weeks later demonstrated resolution of pericholecystic inflammatory changes, nonopacification of the cystic artery and pseudoaneurysm, and coils in place, confirming successful embolization.
